annotationRationale: Complement counting removes prime-free subsets from the total. The multiplication principle counts subsets through include-or-exclude choices, and identifying primes determines the excluded family.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official method, subtracting prime-free subsets from all subsets, with the power-of-two counts and unique counting explained.

review.mathCheck: There are \(2^8=256\) subsets. The prime-free subsets use only 4, 6, 8 and 9, giving \(2^4=16\), including the empty set. Their complement has \(256-16=240\) members, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of the first MAA solution 5. It additionally explains why include-or-exclude choices count every subset exactly once.
review.annotationCheck: Complement counting and the multiplication principle are appropriately assessed; prime classification is supporting knowledge. The two families exhaust all subsets without overlap.
